app.name: Outpost Academy
app.tagline: Every choice has a cost. See why.

common.tryAgain: Play again with a new plan

first_day.name: First Day
first_day.intro: Welcome to your Moon base! Four astronauts are counting on you.
first_day.goal: Keep the air machine running and the shield strong.
first_day.tip: Every day you get energy blocks. Share them wisely!
first_day.fact: An astronaut needs a bit less than 1 kilogram of oxygen every day.
first_day.askKid: Which system would you protect first, and why?
first_day.learn: Everything on a base runs on limited energy, so every choice has a cost.

long_night.name: Long Night
long_night.intro: Night is coming. The Sun will hide for days.
long_night.goal: Save energy in the battery before the lights go out.
long_night.tip: No sunlight means no new blocks. Plan ahead!
long_night.fact: On the Moon, one night lasts about two weeks on Earth.
long_night.askKid: How many days of energy should we save?
long_night.learn: Planning ahead: what you save today prevents problems tomorrow.

storm_watch.name: Storm Watch
storm_watch.intro: A storm of space particles may reach the base.
storm_watch.goal: Make the shield strong before the storm arrives.
storm_watch.tip: The forecast shows when the storm comes. Use it!
storm_watch.fact: NASA scientists track solar flares every day.
storm_watch.askKid: Why is it smart to prepare before the storm?
storm_watch.learn: Real space weather forecasts give crews time to prepare. Protection costs energy that you cannot use elsewhere.

green_thumb.name: Green Thumb
green_thumb.intro: Fresh food needs a garden. Time to build a greenhouse!
green_thumb.goal: Grow food without leaving the base in the dark.
green_thumb.tip: Plant lamps use energy. Balance light, air and shield.
green_thumb.fact: Astronauts on the space station have grown and eaten lettuce.
green_thumb.askKid: What would you give up for a bigger harvest?
green_thumb.learn: Growing food takes energy and water, so every system competes for the same resources.

thirsty_base.name: Thirsty Base
thirsty_base.intro: Water is the base lifeline. Time to find it and save it.
thirsty_base.goal: Share water between drinking, plants and air.
thirsty_base.tip: Mining ice costs energy. Recycling saves it.
thirsty_base.fact: Astronauts recycle most of their water, even from sweat and breath.
thirsty_base.askKid: Where does water matter most on a base?
thirsty_base.learn: Water connects all the other systems, so a shortage spreads quickly.

mars_landing.name: Hello, Mars
mars_landing.intro: You have landed on Mars! The sky changes every day, and the weather card tells you what is coming.
mars_landing.goal: Keep the crew safe and learn to read the Mars weather.
mars_landing.tip: Look at the weather card. Cold, dust and dust devils change how much energy you get.
mars_landing.fact: A day on Mars, called a sol, lasts about 24 hours and 40 minutes.
mars_landing.askKid: How is the weather on Mars different from the weather at home?
mars_landing.learn: On Mars the Sun is weaker and the weather changes the energy you get. Planning with the forecast is how real crews work.

mars_cold.name: Frozen Sols
mars_cold.intro: A series of very cold days is coming. Heaters will take part of your energy.
mars_cold.goal: Keep the greenhouse alive while the cold lasts.
mars_cold.tip: On cold days you get 1 block less and the plants grow slower. Give the greenhouse a block.
mars_cold.fact: Mars is a cold desert world: about minus 60 degrees Celsius on average.
mars_cold.askKid: What would you do first when the temperature drops?
mars_cold.learn: Heating costs energy, and energy is limited. Cold hits several systems at once.

mars_dust.name: Dust Season
mars_dust.intro: It is dust season. The sky is orange and the Sun is dim. A solar storm is also coming at the end.
mars_dust.goal: Get through the dusty days and have a strong shield for the storm.
mars_dust.tip: On dusty days only half of the sunlight arrives. A dust devil may clean the panels for free.
mars_dust.fact: Wind and dust devils have cleaned the solar panels of real Mars rovers.
mars_dust.askKid: Why is dust a problem for solar panels?
mars_dust.learn: Mars dust dims the sunlight and sticks to machines. Mars also has thin air, so the shield matters even more.

mars_global.name: Global Dust Storm
mars_global.intro: A dust storm grows until it covers the whole planet. For days almost no sunlight will reach the base.
mars_global.goal: Fill the battery before the storm and make it last.
mars_global.tip: Global storm days give almost no blocks. The battery holds up to 8, so charge it first.
mars_global.fact: In 2018 a planet-wide dust storm ended the mission of the Opportunity rover.
mars_global.askKid: How many days of energy should we save before the storm?
mars_global.learn: When the Sun disappears, only stored energy counts. Good plans save energy before trouble arrives.

mars_commander.name: Mars Commander
mars_commander.intro: This is your final mission. Cold, dust, a dust devil, a global storm and a solar storm are all coming.
mars_commander.goal: Use everything you learned to bring all four crew members home safe.
mars_commander.tip: Read the weather card every day. Save energy before bad weather and build the shield before the solar storm.
mars_commander.fact: Radio messages between Earth and Mars take up to about 20 minutes each way.
mars_commander.askKid: Which day will be the hardest, and how will you get ready?
mars_commander.learn: Real Mars crews plan around weather, energy and distance from Earth. You just did the same.

food_short.why: The crew got weak without food.

air_empty.title: The air ran out
air_empty.why: Without fresh air the crew lost a heart.

micro_hit.title: A space rock hit the shield
micro_hit.why: Tiny rocks can damage the shield, so keep it strong.

storm_weak_shield.title: The shield was too weak
storm_weak_shield.why: A weak shield lets space particles reach the crew.

storm_ok.title: The shield held
storm_ok.why: Strong shielding kept the crew safe.

clean_air_cost.title: Cleaning the panels used air
clean_air_cost.why: Going outside to clean costs air, but it gives more energy tomorrow.

decision_patch.why: You chose between a stronger shield and new science.

decision_solar.why: You chose between more energy tomorrow and saving air.

drone_used.why: The drone did the science, so nobody had to go outside and breathe extra air.

radio_used.title: You called Earth
radio_used.why: Earth helped the weakest system, but the call used a block of energy.

mars_cold.title: A cold sol on Mars
mars_cold.why: Heaters took some energy and the plants grew slower. Cold days are hard on a base.

mars_dusty.title: Dust dimmed the Sun
mars_dusty.why: Dust in the Martian sky blocked half of the sunlight, so the panels made less energy.

mars_global.title: A global dust storm
mars_global.why: Dust covered the whole planet. Almost no sunlight reached the panels, so the battery had to carry the base.

mars_devil.title: A dust devil cleaned the panels
mars_devil.why: A whirlwind swept the dust off the panels for free. Real Mars rovers were cleaned like this too.

decision_moon_soil.title: Mission Control decision: moon soil walls
decision_moon_soil.why: You chose between a stronger shield and saving energy.

decision_mars_signal.title: Mission Control decision: the signal delay

howTo.title: How to play
howTo.s1: Look at the yellow squares: that is your energy for today.
howTo.s2: Tap + on a machine to give it energy. The Air machine always needs 2.
howTo.s3: Press End day. Watch the hearts: they show if your crew is safe.

together.title: Co-pilot corner
together.what: A grown-up and a child play as a team. The child taps the blocks (Pilot). The grown-up reads the clues and asks questions (Co-pilot).
together.roles: Pilot: the child taps + and −. Co-pilot: the grown-up reads aloud and asks.

q.air: Ask: What happens if the air machine does not get its 2 blocks?
q.waste: Ask: Why is it a pity to waste energy blocks? Where could they go instead?
q.storm: Ask: The storm comes tomorrow. How strong should the shield be, and why?
q.micro: Ask: What could a space rock do to the shield? How can you get ready?
q.ok: Ask: What do you think will happen when you press End day? Say your guess, then check the report.

together.after: Talk about it: What surprised you? What will you change tomorrow?
together.debrief: Talk about it: What would you do differently next time?

decision.title: Message from Mission Control
decision.pick: Choose one. Each choice gains something and costs something.

airlock.text: The air filters can get a deep check today.
airlock.aWhy: The air is fresher, but the check uses a block tomorrow.
airlock.bWhy: You save a block, but the air gets a little worse.

patch.text: A small crack was found near the shield.
patch.aWhy: The shield is stronger, but the walk outside used air.
patch.bWhy: You learned something new, but the shield got weaker.

rest.text: The crew is tired after a long day.
rest.aWhy: The crew feels better, but resting costs a block tomorrow.
rest.bWhy: You get an extra block, but the tired crew wastes some air.

solar.text: Dust is on the solar panels.
solar.aWhy: More energy tomorrow, but the walk used air.
solar.bWhy: Fresher air inside, but less energy tomorrow.

ice.text: Your drill found ice under the ground.
ice.a: Melt a lot of ice now
ice.aWhy: You get more water, but the melter uses a block tomorrow.
ice.bWhy: You save a block, but there is less water.

seeds.text: The new seeds are ready to plant.
seeds.aWhy: More food soon, but the crew had no time to check the air filters.
seeds.bWhy: The air filters get checked, but the garden grows slower.

moon_soil.text: There is a big pile of moon soil next to the base.
moon_soil.aWhy: Moon soil blocks space particles, but the digger used a block.
moon_soil.bWhy: You save a block, but the walls are less protected.

mars_signal.text: You ask Earth for advice. A message takes up to about 20 minutes each way.
mars_signal.aWhy: You learn something new, but waiting cost a block.
mars_signal.bWhy: A quick fix for the air, but the guess weakened the shield.

mars_rover.text: The crew can drive the pressurized rover to a far rock.
mars_rover.aWhy: New science, but the trip used air.
mars_rover.bWhy: You save energy, but nobody checked the shield.

quiz.title: Bonus science question
quiz.wrong: Not this time. No penalty, now you know!

oxygen.q: About how much oxygen does one astronaut breathe each day?
oxygen.why: NASA life support planning uses a bit less than 1 kg of oxygen per person per day.

moxie.q: What did the MOXIE experiment on Mars make?
moxie.why: MOXIE made oxygen from Martian air on the Perseverance rover.

flare.q: Which solar flare class is the strongest?
flare.why: Flares are ranked A, B, C, M, X. X is the strongest.

delay.q: A message from Mars to Earth can take up to about...
delay.why: Radio signals travel at light speed, but Mars is far away: up to about 20 minutes one way.

moon_gravity.q: How strong is gravity on the Moon compared with Earth?
moon_gravity.why: Moon gravity is about one sixth of Earth's, so astronauts bounce when they walk.

moon_night.q: How long does one night last on the Moon?
moon_night.why: A Moon day and night together last about 29.5 Earth days, so the night is about two weeks long.

moon_air.q: Why do astronauts wear spacesuits on the Moon?
o: The Moon has almost no air
moon_air.why: The Moon has almost no atmosphere, so people cannot breathe there and need a suit with air.

moon_ice.q: Where has NASA found water ice on the Moon?
o: In dark craters near the poles
In the middle of the sea of dust
moon_ice.why: Some craters near the poles never get sunlight. It is so cold there that water ice can stay frozen.

moon_artemis.q: What is the name of NASA's program to send people back to the Moon?
moon_artemis.why: Artemis is NASA's program to return astronauts to the Moon and prepare for Mars.

moon_walkers.q: How many people have walked on the Moon so far?
moon_walkers.why: Twelve astronauts walked on the Moon during the Apollo missions.

moon_signal.q: How long does a radio message take to travel from Earth to the Moon?
o: There is no delay at all
moon_signal.why: Radio travels at the speed of light. The Moon is close, so a message arrives in about one second.

moon_sunset.q: What happens to the temperature when the Sun sets on the Moon?
moon_sunset.why: The Moon has almost no air to hold heat, so the surface cools down very fast after sunset.

moon_craters.q: What made most of the craters on the Moon?
moon_craters.why: With almost no air and no rain, craters stay for billions of years. Most were made by space rocks.

moon_dust.q: Why is moon dust a problem for machines and suits?
o: It is sharp and sticks to everything
moon_dust.why: Moon dust is sharp and clingy. Apollo astronauts found that it wore out suits and got into joints.

moon_solar.q: Why is the lunar night a problem for solar power?
o: The Sun is hidden, so panels make no energy
moon_solar.why: Solar panels need sunlight. During the long night a base must live on stored energy.

moon_shield.q: What can help protect a Moon base from space radiation?
o: Covering it with moon soil or water
moon_shield.why: Thick layers of material, like moon soil or water, can absorb many space particles.

mars_sol.q: How long is one day on Mars, called a sol?
mars_sol.why: A sol is about 24 hours and 40 minutes, only a little longer than an Earth day.

o: It is very close to the Sun
mars_red.why: Mars dust has a lot of iron that has rusted. That is why the planet looks red-orange.

mars_airgas.q: What gas is most of the air on Mars made of?
mars_airgas.why: Martian air is mostly carbon dioxide, so people cannot breathe it.

mars_thin.q: Compared with Earth, the air on Mars is...
mars_thin.why: The air on Mars is very thin. It holds little heat and gives little protection from space.

mars_chill.q: Is Mars warmer or colder than Earth?
mars_chill.why: Mars is a cold desert. The average temperature is about minus 60 degrees Celsius.

mars_gravity.q: How strong is gravity on Mars compared with Earth?
mars_gravity.why: Gravity on Mars is about 38 percent of Earth's. You would weigh much less there.

mars_year.q: How long is one year on Mars?
mars_year.why: Mars is farther from the Sun, so it needs about 687 Earth days to go around it once.

mars_devilq.q: What can clean dust off a rover's solar panels on Mars?
o: A gust of wind, like a dust devil
mars_devilq.why: Mars has no rain, but wind gusts and dust devils have blown dust off the panels of real rovers.

mars_opportunity.q: Why did the Opportunity rover go quiet in 2018?
o: A planet-wide dust storm hid the Sun
It ran out of rocket fuel
mars_opportunity.why: A huge dust storm blocked the sunlight, so the rover's solar panels could not recharge its batteries.

mars_helicopter.q: Ingenuity was the first helicopter to fly on which world besides Earth?
mars_helicopter.why: Ingenuity flew on Mars in 2021. The air there is so thin that its blades had to spin very fast.

mars_moons.q: How many moons does Mars have?
mars_moons.why: Mars has two small moons, Phobos and Deimos.

mars_water.q: Where is most of the water on Mars today?
o: Frozen as ice, at the poles and underground
mars_water.why: Today Mars water is mostly ice. That ice is a possible source of water for future crews.

mars_trip.q: About how long does a trip from Earth to Mars take with today's rockets?
mars_trip.why: With today's rockets the trip takes about six to nine months, depending on when you leave.

mars_radiation.q: Why is radiation a risk for people on the surface of Mars?
o: Mars is too close to the Sun
Thin air and no global magnetic field give little protection
mars_radiation.why: Earth's magnetic field and thick air protect us. Mars has much less of both, so a base needs a shield.

mars_volcano.q: What is the giant volcano on Mars called?
mars_volcano.why: Olympus Mons is the tallest known volcano in our solar system.

iss_orbit.q: How often does the space station fly around the Earth?
iss_orbit.why: The station goes very fast, so its crew sees about 16 sunrises every day.

iss_float.q: Why do astronauts float inside the space station?
o: There is no gravity up there
They are in constant free fall around Earth
iss_float.why: Gravity is still strong there. The station and the crew are falling around Earth together, so they feel weightless.

iss_water.q: What do astronauts on the space station do with used water?
o: Clean it and use it again
Pour it on the plants only
iss_water.why: The station recycles most of its water, even from sweat and breath, because bringing water from Earth is very expensive.

iss_lettuce.q: What did astronauts grow and eat on the space station?
iss_lettuce.why: Astronauts grew red romaine lettuce in the Veggie garden and ate it fresh.

sun_light.q: How long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
sun_light.why: Light from the Sun travels about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach us.

sun_cme.q: What is a coronal mass ejection?
o: A huge cloud of particles thrown out by the Sun
sun_cme.why: It is a giant cloud of charged particles that the Sun throws into space. NASA watches for them every day.

sun_aurora.q: What makes the colorful auroras near Earth's poles?
o: Particles from the Sun hitting the air
sun_aurora.why: Particles from the Sun hit gases high in our air and make them glow.

plants_base.q: Why are plants useful on a space base?
o: They can give food and fresh oxygen
plants_base.why: Plants can make food and oxygen. That is why NASA tests gardens in space.

facts.title: Did you know?
facts.oxygen: One astronaut breathes almost 1 kilogram of oxygen every day.
facts.flare: Solar flares are ranked A, B, C, M and X. Each letter is about 10 times stronger than the one before.
facts.moxie: A small machine on Mars called MOXIE made oxygen from the Martian air.
facts.delay: A radio message from Mars to Earth can take up to about 20 minutes.
facts.sol: One day on Mars, called a sol, lasts about 24 hours and 40 minutes.
facts.marsair: Mars has very thin air, made mostly of carbon dioxide, so people cannot breathe it.
facts.dustdevil: Swirling dust devils on Mars have blown the dust off the solar panels of rovers.
facts.marsyear: A year on Mars lasts about 687 Earth days, almost twice as long as ours.
